s: Which one of the following statements does not apply to the system of Subsidiary Alliance introduced by Lord Wellesley?
o: To maintain a large standing army at others expense
To keep India safe from Napoleonic danger
To secure a fixed income for the Company
To establish British paramountcy over the Indian States
x: Statement (c) does not apply to the system of Subsidiary Alliance: The primary objective was to establish military and political dominance rather than ensuring a stable revenue for the Company. Though the Subsidiary Alliance system was quite old, Wellesley gave it a definite shape. Under the system, the ruler of the allied Indian state was compelled to accept the permanent stationing of a British force within his territory and to pay a subsidy for its maintenance. The ruler, unable to pay the expenses, had to cede a part of his kingdom to the British. The British agreed to defend the ruler from his enemies. They also controlled the defence and foreign relations of the protected ally. In return, the Indian ruler of the protected state should keep a British Resident at his court and disband his own army.  Indian rulers should not employ Europeans in their service without the approval of the British.  Indian rulers should not negotiate with any other Indian ruler without consulting the Governor-General. • The System of Subsidiary Alliance was also aimed at preventing French influence (the Napoleonic threat) from entering India. This system enabled the British to uphold a substantial army, with the financial burden falling Modern Indian History PMF IAS IH – 154 on the local rulers (it helped the British to have paramountcy over the Indian States), and was not implemented for securing a fixed income for the East India Company.

s: Which one of the following statements does not apply to the system of Subsidiary Alliance introduced by Lord Wellesley?
o: To maintain a large standing army at other’s expense
To keep India safe from Napoleonic danger
To secure a fixed income for the company
To establish British paramountcy over the Indian States
x: Governor-General Lord Wellesley came to India in 1798 A.D. at a time when the British were locked in a life and death struggle with France all over the world. The fear of Napoleon haunted the Britishers everywhere. To achieve his political aims, Wellesley relied on the system of Subsidiary Alliance. While the practice of helping Indian rulers with a paid British force was quite old, it was given shape by Wellesley who used it to sub-ordinate the Indian states to the paramountcy of the company. Under the subsidiary Alliance system, the ruler of the allying state was compelled to accept the permanent stationing of a British force within his territory and to pay a subsidy for its maintenance. However, to secure a fixed income for the company was not under the agenda of the Subsidiary Alliance.

s:
Statement (A): Moturpha is a salt tax levied by the British East India Company.
Statement (B): The revenue collected by the British East India Company from the Zamindars is called Peshcush.
x:
Statement (A) is false. Moturpha was not a salt tax. It was a professional or trade tax imposed on artisans, craftsmen, traders and occupational groups by the British East India Company. The salt tax was a separate levy imposed on the manufacture and sale of salt.
Statement (B) is true. Peshcush refers to the fixed annual tribute or land revenue paid by Zamindars to the British East India Company under the Zamindari system. It became an important source of revenue during British rule in the Madras Presidency. Therefore, Statement (A) is false and Statement (B) is true. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Moturpha – Tax on professions, trades and occupations.
• Peshcush – Fixed revenue paid by Zamindars to the British.

s: Who said that the project named Ramapada Sagaram near Polavaram will be built?
x:
Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy, one of the distinguished irrigation engineers of Andhra, strongly advocated the construction of a major irrigation project across the Godavari River near Polavaram. He proposed that the project be named "Ramapada Sagaram." His proposal highlighted the enormous irrigation potential of the Godavari River and emphasized that its waters could transform the drought-prone regions of Andhra through irrigation, drinking water supply and hydroelectric generation. Although Sir Arthur Cotton pioneered irrigation development through the construction of the Dowleswaram Anicut, the proposal to build the Polavaram project as Ramapada Sagaram is associated with Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy. Later, Dr. K. L. Rao also supported the development of India's river valley projects and interlinking of rivers, but the original proposal carrying the name Ramapada Sagaram is credited to Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Ramapada Sagaram – Proposed near Polavaram
• Proposed by – Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy
• Present Project – Polavaram Multipurpose Project

G. N. Taylor, who served as the Sub-Collector of Rajahmundry, played an important role in promoting modern education in Andhra. He established several Anglo-Vernacular schools in different parts of the Godavari region to provide education in both English and Telugu. His educational reforms significantly contributed to the spread of modern learning and produced many educated leaders in Andhra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
